subject: Request: Rolling maintenance — temporary P1/P2 on-call coverage change
messages:
From: Lina Ortega <lina@greenfield.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T08:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Rolling maintenance — temporary P1/P2 on-call coverage change

Hi Karthik, Marissa, Jonas,

We’re planning a month-long staggered maintenance window across our EMEA clusters starting 2026-12-05 to 2027-01-04 to upgrade our networking stack. During this period, we need a temporary change to our P1/P2 response commitments: specifically, a carve-in that shifts overnight P2 responses to business-hours-only for the affected clusters and a limited delay allowance for P1 acknowledgements during the hourly rolling reboot (estimated 15–20 minutes per cluster).

We know this is a deviation from the current SLA, so we’re requesting an exception and are happy to accept tighter escalation handoffs, additional on-call paging, or a short credit for elevated risk. Attached is our maintenance plan and a sketch of the outages and time buckets per region.

Goal: get an agreement on a temporary SLA amendment + an agreed runbook for escalations during the maintenance window. Can we get internal approval by EOD 2026-12-01?

Thanks,
Lina Ortega
Head of Platform Ops | Greenfield AI
platform-ops@greenfield.ai

Attachments: greenfield_rolling_maintenance_plan.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortega <lina@greenfield.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Rolling maintenance — temporary P1/P2 on-call coverage change

Lina — thanks for the clear plan. I’ve skimmed the attachment and the per-cluster windows look manageable, but we need to lock two things before we can sign off:

1) A mutual action plan (MAP) that includes an agreed daily status cadence and a single point of contact during each rolling hour.
2) A short runbook that defines the exact paging thresholds and automatic fallback to our secondary region.

From Redwood’s side, I can route a temporary SLA amendment: we can authorize a conditional tolerance for P1 acknowledgement up to 15 minutes during the brief reboot window per cluster (not to exceed 3 reboots per day per cluster), and convert overnight P2s to next-business-hours responses provided Greenfield implements the agreed handoff cadence and we have a signed MAP. This would be timeboxed to 2026-12-05 through 2027-01-04. Any longer and we’ll need to revisit.

I’m looping in Marissa for commercial signoff (credits/terms) and Jonas to draft the operational runbook and escalation path.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: confirm commercial concessions (credits vs. flat service amendment).
- Jonas: draft a short runbook and the emergency fallback steps by 2026-12-01.
- Lina: confirm the daily status check time and single POC rotation.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortega <lina@greenfield.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Rolling maintenance — temporary P1/P2 on-call coverage change

Lina — appreciate the early notice and the detailed plan. From a commercial perspective we can offer a limited credit equal to 3% of expected monthly usage for December (applied to the Jan invoice) in exchange for the MAP and the runbook commitments Karthik outlined. That’s our standard remedy for short-term, customer-requested SLA relaxations.

Two clarifications:
- The credit covers the timeboxed window only (2026-12-05 to 2027-01-04).
- We need a signed amendment that lists: maintenance dates, exact response-time tolerances, and the MAP signatories.

If that works, I’ll prepare the amendment draft. Can Lina or someone on your legal/ops team confirm the POC rotation (name + contact) by 2026-12-01 COB?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_sla_amendment_draft.docx (placeholder)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortega <lina@greenfield.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Rolling maintenance — temporary P1/P2 on-call coverage change

Lina / team — following discussions with Karthik and Marissa I’ve reviewed the maintenance windows and the proposed controls. Redwood can approve the requested temporary modification under the following conditions (please see attached runbook):

1) MAP: Daily status check at 09:00 UTC with the on-call POC for that day listed in the MAP.
2) Paging thresholds: P1 = page immediately; acknowledgement window extended to 15 minutes ONLY during the per-cluster reboot minute window (documented in the MAP). P2 = deferred to next business day for affected clusters between 22:00–06:00 CET during maintenance.
3) Fallback: Automatic failover to secondary region if two consecutive clusters fail to come out of maintenance within 30 minutes.
4) Observability: Greenfield will enable synthetic checks for the maintenance buckets and share the dashboards with Redwood for the maintenance period.
5) Signed amendment and MAP must be returned by 2026-12-01 23:59 UTC for the exception to be effective.

If those items are accepted, I’ll attach the runbook (runbook_emergency_fallback.md) and we’ll prepare the formal amendment for signature. I’ve pasted the salient section from your maintenance plan below for reference.

On Sat, Nov 28, 2026 at 08:12 Lina Ortega <lina@greenfield.ai> wrote:
> We’re planning a month-long staggered maintenance window across our EMEA clusters starting 2026-12-05 to 2027-01-04 to upgrade our networking stack.
> 
> During this period, we need a temporary change to our P1/P2 response commitments: specifically, a carve-in that shifts overnight P2 responses to business-hours-only for the affected clusters and a limited delay allowance for P1 acknowledgements during the hourly rolling reboot (estimated 15–20 minutes per cluster).
> 
> Attached is our maintenance plan and a sketch of the outages and time buckets per region.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Support Lead, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: runbook_emergency_fallback.md
